title: Last 10-question night — read the item
description: Vote still open. Ten short reads. Tomorrow’s longer quiz stays unstaged until the ballot ends.

questions.question: Caps collected by hand. What is the honest household jar?
options: Caps only — a second grade, saved clean
Caps plus residual food plus foil
Caps left on every bottle
Caps thrown in the film sack
questions.answer: Caps only — a second grade, saved clean
questions.explanation: A jar of caps is a sort. A jar of leftovers is a smell.

questions.question: Coloured bins in a line. You have a rinsed PET bottle. Where?
options: The stream that takes plastic bottles — not every bin
A little into each bin to be fair
The food bin, because it held a drink
No bin — PET cannot be collected
questions.answer: The stream that takes plastic bottles — not every bin
questions.explanation: One item, one home. Fairness is not a pinch in every colour.

questions.question: Bottles gathered, not yet baled. What do you still check?
options: Stranger grades, wet, and leftover food
Whether the photo is pretty
Whether every bottle is a different colour
Whether the bags are from a beach
questions.answer: Stranger grades, wet, and leftover food
questions.explanation: Gathered is a start. Clean same-grade is the product.

questions.question: A mixed waste mountain. What is the first pull?
options: One grade you can name, kept in its own sack
The shiniest item, any material
Everything into one liner
Only the items with labels you like
questions.answer: One grade you can name, kept in its own sack
questions.explanation: Name it, then bag it. A mountain is not a sort.

questions.question: Stacked PET bales under the sky. What must not be inside?
options: A surprise jerry can, film, or a wet food tub
Clear PET bottles
Air that was pressed out
Bands that hold the bale
questions.answer: A surprise jerry can, film, or a wet food tub
questions.explanation: The stack is a promise of PET. Strangers break the promise.

questions.question: Beach fragments, many shapes. Why sort at home instead of waiting for the sand?
options: Whole, dry, named grade still has a buyer
Sand sorts better than hands
Fragments are the most valuable form
The tide returns bottles as new drinks
questions.answer: Whole, dry, named grade still has a buyer
questions.explanation: The beach is late. The kitchen is on time.

questions.question: Marine debris including crates. Is this only a ‘tourist beach’ problem?
options: No — inland drains feed coasts
Yes — only visitors drop plastic
Yes — crates cannot come from a house
No — crates are always local sand
questions.explanation: A highland kitchen and a coast share a road. The drain is the on-ramp.

questions.question: A PP tub and a PET bottle on the same table. Two photos or one?
options: Two — they are different grades
One — both held food or drink
One — both are ‘plastic’
None — tubs cannot be photographed
questions.explanation: Same-grade in one frame. Two materials, two frames.

questions.question: Cloudy HDPE jugs beside a clear PET memory in your head. What do you trust?
options: The wall in your hand, then the triangle
The memory of a water brand
The lid colour only
The shop shelf they sat on
questions.answer: The wall in your hand, then the triangle
questions.explanation: Feel, then read. Brand stories lie more than moulded marks.

questions.question: A river of bottles. Someone says ‘the ocean will handle it.’ What is true?
options: The ocean is downhill of this river, not a bin
The ocean sorts grades for free
Bottles become fish food on purpose
Rivers cannot reach a coast
questions.answer: The ocean is downhill of this river, not a bin
questions.explanation: Downhill is not disposal. Lift it while it is still a bottle.
